name: Left Accelerationism
summary: Left accelerationism holds that capitalism, once a driver of technological change, now stagnates and holds back productive forces, and that the left should seize and repurpose modern technology and infrastructure rather than retreat into localism. It calls for post-capitalist planning, automation, a shorter working week and an unconditional income, pursued through building a new left hegemony, organisation and collectively controlled authority.
scope: The left-wing strand set out in the 2013 Accelerationist Manifesto by Nick Srnicek and Alex Williams and developed in their book Inventing the Future (2015), with Mark Fisher as an influence. It excludes Nick Land's right-wing and neoreactionary accelerationism and the CCRU's earlier aesthetic currents. Because the sources are few and strategic, many statements on social, religious and foreign policy questions are inferred and marked low.

sources.title: Inventing the Future: Postcapitalism and a World Without Work
sources.author: Wikipedia
sources.usedFor: Four demands (automation, shorter week, unconditional income, diminished work ethic), folk politics, hegemony, populist strategy, unions, anti-hierarchy modernity.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Not discussed in the sources; inferred from a post-capitalist, anti-austerity programme that treats neoliberal cuts as the enemy and wants decommodified provision.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Inventing the Future argues that raising labour costs pushes firms to automate, and it wants a better deal for precarious workers, though its own flagship demand is basic income rather than the wage floor.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The manifesto says any post-capitalism needs post-capitalist planning and rejects market-driven development as the vehicle of progress.

public-ownership.rationale: The manifesto wants collectively controlled infrastructure and planning but never specifies nationalisation of named industries, so this is inferred.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Funding an unconditional income and a shorter week implies redistribution from capital, but the sources do not set out tax policy.

unions-good.rationale: The book treats unions as one institution the left must work through and rebuild, while criticising their weakness and narrow defensive role.

property-fundamental.rationale: The manifesto attacks intellectual-property monopolies and aims at a post-capitalist order in which productive property is collectively controlled.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Not a stated focus; the programme targets capitalism itself rather than seeking better regulation of it, so support is mild and inferred.

cut-welfare.rationale: The authors demand a generous unconditional income and reject the work ethic that underlies welfare-dependency arguments.

worker-ownership.rationale: Collective control of production fits the post-capitalist aim, but the sources favour planning and vertical authority more than cooperatives, so it is inferred.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left-wing civil-liberties commitments, with the manifesto's endorsement of secrecy in organising pointing the other way on state power.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; inferred from a broadly libertarian-left, anti-work cultural stance.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: The sources are silent and adherents could split between anti-oppression commitments and free-speech concerns.

strong-leader.rationale: The manifesto wants collective, legitimate vertical authority rather than a personal leader bypassing institutions.

state-harmful.rationale: The manifesto explicitly rejects horizontalism and calls for collectively controlled vertical authority, treating the state as a tool to be captured.

limit-guns.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from mainstream left positions.

empower-police-military.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the left's opposition to coercive state expansion under neoliberalism.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from the post-work, anti-work-ethic stance and general left social liberalism.

decide-locally.rationale: The manifesto condemns the folk politics of localism and says global abstract forces cannot be confronted at local scale.

rehabilitation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left universalism and opposition to neoliberal punitive politics.

traditional-family.rationale: The book calls for a modernity that dismantles gender hierarchies, and the manifesto criticises the Fordist family hierarchy.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: The authors want a new modernity dismantling gender and race hierarchies, which clearly includes legal equality for same-sex couples.

abortion-legal.rationale: Following from the aim of dismantling gender hierarchies; the sources do not discuss abortion itself.

more-religion-public.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a secular Promethean outlook.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: The authors' vision of modernity explicitly dismantles race hierarchies, though they give no concrete programme.

gender-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed directly; the Promethean claim that there are no immutable givens suggests agreement.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: The manifesto criticises national hierarchies of the Fordist era and wants a globalised post-capitalism, so national-cultural preservation is not a goal.

gradual-change.rationale: The manifesto calls for accelerating beyond capitalism and rejects reactive, incremental politics.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from internationalism and the aim of a global post-capitalism.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: The manifesto wants global-scale politics, but it offers no view on the UN or similar bodies and adherents would be wary of liberal institutions.

free-trade.rationale: Not addressed directly; they reject neoliberalism as the vehicle of progress, but they do not defend protectionism either.

nation-first.rationale: The manifesto frames the choice as globalised post-capitalism or fragmentation and wants universal, not national, projects.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: The sources never address military intervention; left internationalism and anti-imperialism pull in opposite directions.

open-borders.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from universalism and a global post-capitalism, with the book's stress on universal human values.

limit-growth.rationale: They reject limits and localist degrowth, arguing technological and economic acceleration must continue under collective control, while treating climate collapse as the great threat.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: The manifesto calls climate breakdown the most critical threat and says the choice is globalised post-capitalism or fragmentation.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: They are Promethean about technology yet the manifesto warns never to believe technology alone will save us, so agreement is moderate.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from their pro-technology, climate-urgent outlook.

revolution-justified.rationale: The manifesto speaks of conflict and a break with capitalism but is silent on violent revolution, preferring hegemonic and institutional strategy.

experts-over-public.rationale: They value economic modelling and expertise but insist democracy means collective self-mastery, so adherents are split.

central-planning.rationale: The manifesto says any post-capitalism will require post-capitalist planning and cites Cybersyn and Soviet cybernetics as experiments to learn from.

socialized-markets.rationale: Not addressed; the sources favour planning, though some post-capitalist visions admit market elements.

land-value-tax.rationale: Not addressed and not a theme of the movement.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inferred from the redistributive, anti-concentration aims; the sources do not discuss inheritance.

basic-income.rationale: A generous, unconditional income for all is one of the four demands of Inventing the Future.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Not addressed; their globalist, anti-localist outlook cuts against protectionism, though they also oppose neoliberal trade rules.

state-directs-investment.rationale: Post-capitalist planning and repurposing existing infrastructure imply the state steering investment toward collectively chosen goals.

widespread-small-property.rationale: The manifesto's collective, large-scale planning is opposed to localist small-owner economies.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Their goal is a post-work society with automation and unconditional income, which loosens the wage relation, though the sources stop short of abolishing money.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Market-led money is the opposite of their planning orientation.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Not addressed; they want collectively controlled planning rather than state-recognised class collaboration.

one-party-rule.rationale: They stress vertical authority and organisation but within a democratic hegemonic strategy and an ecology of organisations, not a single ruling party.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Hereditary rule contradicts their commitment to democracy defined as collective self-mastery.

democracy-best.rationale: The manifesto redefines real democracy by its goal of collective self-mastery, so they back democracy but not as mere procedure.

direct-votes.rationale: The manifesto says voting, discussion and assemblies are not sufficient and criticises horizontalism.

workers-councils.rationale: They reject the horizontalism of assembly politics and favour combined vertical and horizontal forms; councils as sole basis is not their line.

right-to-secede.rationale: Not addressed; fragmentation is described as the bad alternative to globalised post-capitalism.

natural-rulers.rationale: They want to dismantle hierarchies and equalise power, which rules out natural aptitude to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: The manifesto frames politics as conflict and says nothing pacifist, though it does not endorse violence either.

war-builds-character.rationale: Nothing in the sources supports militarist ideas; their programme is about emancipation through technology and organisation.

separate-church-state.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from a secular Promethean outlook.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Their rationalist, universalist modernity leaves no place for scriptural law.

private-courts-defense.rationale: They want collectively controlled authority, so privatising law and defence contradicts the programme.

ethnic-nation.rationale: The authors want a modernity dismantling race hierarchies and universal in scope.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The manifesto treats politics as riven with conflict and works within a Marxist frame, but it is more about the present strategy than a general theory of history.

equal-outcomes.rationale: Inferred from a post-capitalist, anti-hierarchy programme with a generous unconditional income.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Not addressed; their critique of localism cuts against it while their anti-hierarchy aims favour it.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left anti-imperialism and the manifesto's criticism of imperial hierarchies.

civilizational-union.rationale: Not addressed; they favour global rather than civilisational blocs.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Neoliberal individualism is their target, and collective self-mastery is their ethic.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from universalist left commitments to rights.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Not discussed; they stress mastery over nature and also take climate collapse seriously.

limit-population.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from their rejection of limits and Malthusian thinking.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: They are Promethean and want to accelerate past capitalism, not abandon industrial modernity.

accelerate-technology.rationale: The movement is named for this: the manifesto calls for accelerating technological and social change beyond capitalism's constraints.

human-enhancement.rationale: Prometheanism rejects immutable givens, implying support for enhancement, though the sources do not discuss it.

algorithmic-government.rationale: They favour economic modelling and computational planning, but also insist democracy means collective self-mastery, so the sources do not settle how far algorithms should decide.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left-libertarian digital politics and the manifesto's note that secrecy has its place.

restore-past-order.rationale: The manifesto rejects nostalgia and Fordism as a model and wants a new future.

results-over-ideology.rationale: They are a self-consciously ideological project building a new hegemony, though pragmatic about tools.

direct-action.rationale: The manifesto criticises the folk politics of direct action and relentless horizontalism as insufficient against global forces.

means-match-ends.rationale: They reject prefigurative politics as folk politics, favouring strategic and sometimes vertical means.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Directly opposed to their Promethean, technological project.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: They want to reduce work and the work ethic, but no source says the division of labour itself should go.

distribute-by-need.rationale: An unconditional generous income and automated abundance point toward distribution by need, though the exact formula is not stated.

production-for-use.rationale: Post-capitalist planning replaces market-driven profit, implying production for social need.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The manifesto works within Marxist critique of capitalism, but it never stresses the labour theory of exploitation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: The manifesto favours vertical authority and hegemony but never endorses proletarian dictatorship.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: The sources do not discuss imperialist war; the manifesto describes capitalism as constraining technology instead.

taxation-theft.rationale: Redistribution via the state funds their programme, so this libertarian claim is rejected.

harm-principle.rationale: Not addressed; adherents have no stated position on limits of state restriction.

individual-rights-only.rationale: They stress collective power and universal human values; group rights are not explicitly addressed.

conscription.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left suspicion of military coercion.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Their politics centres on collective democratic mastery, not exit.

positive-liberty.rationale: Freedom from work through automation and income security is a material conception of freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: They want the left to build influence in media and intellectual institutions, implying those are contestable rather than already dominant over elected power.

hereditarian-race.rationale: They want to dismantle race hierarchies and stand on universal human values.

organic-representation.rationale: Corporate or communal representation clashes with their global, modern democratic aims.

total-state.rationale: They want strong collective authority and planning but not state direction of all life including culture.

national-rebirth.rationale: Their orientation is global and post-capitalist, not national decadence narratives.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal authority has no place in a democratic modernising programme.

bound-labor.rationale: They want less coerced work, not more.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: Fisher and others draw on theory-heavy traditions, but the sources do not take a position on this epistemological claim.

universal-morality.rationale: The authors uphold universal human values within a new modernity.

single-common-good.rationale: The manifesto speaks of collective self-mastery as democracy's goal, but also of conflict among groups, so the answer is split.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left internationalism and anti-nationalism.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: The sources never discuss diasporas or citizenship by return, so no position can be drawn.

revive-national-language.rationale: Not addressed; national cultural projects are not part of their outlook.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Collective control of production and rejection of capitalist hierarchy support democratic workplaces, though planning is the headline.

school-vouchers.rationale: Market-based schooling is a neoliberal programme that they oppose.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: They reject austerity logic and want state-led investment in post-capitalist infrastructure.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom in the market sense is neoliberal doctrine they reject.

rule-by-example.rationale: Their politics is institutional and strategic, not moral exemplarism.

national-self-determination.rationale: Not addressed; adherents would be cool on nationalism but sympathetic to self-determination.

force-without-un.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left anti-militarism.

reason-over-faith.rationale: The Promethean outlook rests on rational mastery of society and nature, although it is not framed as strict rationalism.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Universal unconditional income and universalist values contradict citizens-only welfare.

work-for-welfare.rationale: The four demands include a diminished work ethic and an unconditional income, which directly rejects work requirements.

class-collaboration.rationale: The manifesto speaks of rebuilding class power and conflict, not partnership.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Futurist in tone but the sources never endorse destroying cultural institutions, and the manifesto wants to repurpose rather than destroy platforms.

dominated-front.rationale: The manifesto is about a global post-capitalism, and nothing in it speaks to blocs of states against Western powers.

workers-nation.rationale: They want a globalised politics, not nationally bounded labour.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Dismantling gender hierarchies is part of the vision.

ban-interest.rationale: Not addressed; planning approaches would not centre on banning interest.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Directly opposed to the aim of dismantling race hierarchies.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The manifesto treats the state as a tool to be captured and reoriented, not as inherently bourgeois, but their Marxist inheritance suggests partial agreement.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: They treat climate breakdown as the most critical threat.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: Universalism and the dismantling of hierarchies oppose forced assimilation.

elite-replacement.rationale: A conspiracy claim with no basis in their analysis.

proportional-representation.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left democratic preferences.

national-mission.rationale: Their project is global and anti-hegemonic.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: The aim to dismantle gender hierarchies implies a structural view of them.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: They criticise neoliberal elites, but the sources do not use anti-elite populist framing about corruption.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenic coercion contradicts their universal human values and anti-hierarchy aims.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left commitments.

night-watchman-state.rationale: They want a strong, collectively controlled authority and planning.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: Universal human values and the dismantling of hierarchies imply equal worth.

socialism-one-country.rationale: The manifesto stresses a globalised post-capitalism over a localist or national one, which fits this claim.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Neither the manifesto nor the book discusses settler colonialism, so the answer is left neutral.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Personal-law questions are outside the sources, and universalism and religious pluralism pull in different directions.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from secular liberal-left views.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Religiously motivated bans are alien to a secular technological programme.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The sources do not discuss socialist states under siege.

consent-of-governed.rationale: Not stated; their redefinition of democracy as collective self-mastery is compatible.

trade-surplus.rationale: Mercantilist goals are not part of their programme.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: The manifesto treats politics as conflict and endorses state authority, which is incompatible with a non-aggression principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: The manifesto argues capitalism's competition now constrains technology, and favours collective planning.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: Neither source addresses limits on party competition, so no position is drawn.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Not stated, but their anti-hierarchy and collective self-mastery outlook is compatible.

separated-powers.rationale: Not addressed; they want legitimate vertical authority but say nothing on separation of powers.

vanguard-party.rationale: The manifesto wants vertical authority and an organised ecology of groups but also a broad populist coalition, and no source commits to a disciplined vanguard.

priority-to-poor.rationale: A programme of generous income and shorter work focuses on the precarious and unemployed.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from opposition to privatisation of public goods.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: They want to strengthen labour's collective power.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: Their analysis blames capitalism, not population.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Not addressed; their stress on vertical authority argues against it.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left civil-liberties commitments.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with planning, but inferred.

party-controls-media.rationale: They want the left to reform and build media influence, not state control of it.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: The sources say nothing about pay of elected officials.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: They favour vertical authority in organisation but the sources do not specify party discipline.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: They want global-scale politics but have no stated view of the EU, which they would see as neoliberal.

head-commands-forces.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from their preference for collectively controlled authority.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: The sources do not discuss interstate war or the Leninist slogan of revolutionary defeatism.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Executive term rules are not discussed in the manifesto or the book.

recall-officials.rationale: The sources do not discuss recall of elected officials, and their stress on vertical authority leaves it open.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: Military alliances are not discussed in the sources.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Not addressed; mass home ownership schemes are not part of their programme.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Their project is techno-modernist and urban, opposing localist nostalgia.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: National division is not a topic in the manifesto or the book.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: They want the left to build intellectual institutions and hegemony, not attack them.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Universal human values are stressed, but no source rules on cultural hierarchy; adherents would split.

death-penalty.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from left humanism.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with their commitment to dismantling gender hierarchies.

minority-language-support.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with anti-hierarchy aims.

religious-exemptions.rationale: Exemptions from general law for religious minorities are not discussed in the sources.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from Promethean experimentation.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with their anti-austerity stance.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Inferred from the post-capitalist focus on economic transformation.

constituent-assembly.rationale: Constitution writing is not discussed; the strategy centres on hegemony and organisation.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: The manifesto's democracy is defined by collective mastery; authoritarian developmentalism is not endorsed.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Head-of-state selection is not discussed in the sources.

central-bank-independence.rationale: The independent-central-bank model is neoliberal, which they oppose.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Their aim of collective control of productive property fits this subordination of property to social ends.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: They cite Soviet cybernetics as an experiment to learn from but the sources do not characterise the USSR.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Climate seriousness points toward it, but their Promethean stance dislikes brakes on technology.

collective-defense.rationale: Military alliance guarantees are not discussed in the sources.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: Annexation and occupation are not discussed in the sources.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: The role of a head of state is not discussed in the sources.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: Secession and the use of force against it are not discussed in the sources.

region-keeps-system.rationale: Regional autonomy arrangements such as one-country-two-systems are not discussed in the sources.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Redistribution via progressive taxation is implied by an unconditional income.

character-from-environment.rationale: The Promethean rejection of immutable givens fits environmental malleability.

space-expansion.rationale: Prometheanism is about mastery beyond natural limits, but the sources do not mention space.

mixed-constitution.rationale: Classical constitutional theory is outside the sources, so no position is drawn.

equal-parenting.rationale: Custody law is not discussed; gender-equality aims could cut either way on a default presumption.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: Their sources concern the move beyond capitalism, not conflicts inside a socialist society.

land-redistribution.rationale: Not addressed; not an agrarian movement.

refugee-return.rationale: Refugee return rights are not discussed in the sources.

women-must-cover.rationale: Contradicts the dismantling of gender hierarchies.

common-currency.rationale: Currency unions are not discussed in the sources.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Minority cultural self-government is not discussed in the sources.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: Minority strategy between emigration and local struggle is not discussed in the sources.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: The manifesto's focus on productive forces and the material platform reflects a historical-materialist view.

ban-cartels.rationale: Not addressed; they want capitalism overcome, not made more competitive.

no-bailouts.rationale: Not addressed; adherents oppose bailouts of banks but also austerity logic.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: The role of courts against majorities is not discussed in the sources.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with dismantling gender hierarchies.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: Opposite of their globalised post-capitalist aim.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with global-scale regulation.

moral-incentives.rationale: They want to diminish the work ethic, which cuts against moral incentives, but also collective duty; no source rules.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Their strategy is hegemonic and institutional, not foco-style.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Colonial tutelage contradicts their stance against imperial hierarchies.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Their anti-racism implies support for active measures, but sources are silent on affirmative action.

public-money-creation.rationale: Not addressed; consistent with planning and anti-neoliberalism.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: The manifesto argues capitalism is stagnating and now constrains productive forces.

delink-world-market.rationale: The manifesto favours global post-capitalism, not delinking.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Their sources describe precarity and a fragmented working class but do not discuss rich-country workers sharing imperial profits.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: Constitutional rights entrenchment is not discussed in the sources.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: Colonial treaties are not discussed in the sources.

elective-rulers.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from democratic commitments.

minority-veto.rationale: The manifesto criticises horizontalist consensus politics.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: The right to resist a lawless ruler is not discussed in the sources.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary versus monarchical authority is not discussed in the sources.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed; inferred from general left values.

animal-use-humane.rationale: Animal use for food or research is not discussed in the sources.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Paternalist duty of elites is not their approach; they want structural change.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: The manifesto is a call for engaged strategic politics.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Fisher's critique of capitalist realism holds that capitalist culture reproduces the existing order.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: The book builds on the Gramscian idea of hegemony, citing neoliberalism's cultural victory.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: Dependency theory is not discussed in the sources, which focus on capitalism's stagnation in the developed world.

party-own-road.rationale: The sources say nothing about relations between national parties; their global orientation and their organisational pluralism leave adherents split.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Their stress on a globalised post-capitalism and shared technological infrastructure runs against autarkic national development.

return-lost-territory.rationale: Irredentism is a nationalist programme that sits poorly with their internationalism, though the sources never raise it.

indigenous-political-leadership.rationale: Anti-hierarchy aims suggest sympathy for dismantling colonial hierarchies, but their universalism opposes ruling by descent group.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: Their commitment to dismantling race hierarchies fits, though constitutional design is not discussed.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: They draw on Soviet cybernetics as a source of lessons, so equating communism with fascism is unlikely, though not stated.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Revisionism of this kind conflicts with their stance against race hierarchies.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Inferred from their anti-hierarchy outlook, since the sources say nothing on monuments.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources discuss dismantling gender hierarchies, not men's disadvantages, so adherents could differ.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: Inferred from a structural view of gender hierarchy; the sources do not discuss it.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: They stress universal human values and a single global modernity.

military-guardian-role.rationale: A political army contradicts collectively controlled legitimate authority under democratic aims.

paid-care-work.rationale: Reducing the work ethic and demanding an unconditional income rather than wages for housework; sympathy for recognising care work is inferred.

filial-duty.rationale: Traditional family obligation is part of the family hierarchy they criticise.

office-by-exam.rationale: The manifesto values expertise and modelling but says nothing on civil-service selection.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Follows from the dismantling of gender and family hierarchies.

recallable-delegates.rationale: They favour vertical authority, which cuts against binding mandates, yet also democratic control; sources are silent.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Privatised pensions are a neoliberal measure that they reject.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Not discussed; collective control of production fits partly, but they do not address land.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Constitutional budget rules are not discussed in their sources.

single-official-language.rationale: Universalism does not require a single language; inferred.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Land protectionism is alien to a globalist programme.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Their structural view of racial and gender hierarchy suggests sympathy, though they give no legal analysis.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: They call for reducing work and its ethic and for post-scarcity abundance, criticising capitalist work-and-consume life.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from left anti-imperialism.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: Their internationalism and anti-hierarchy aims reject great-power coercion of allies.

corporate-influence.rationale: They oppose neoliberal hegemony, whose success they trace to think tanks and corporate-friendly policy making.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from civil-liberties and internationalist leanings.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: A post-work vision is not pronatalist; inferred, as the sources never discuss population policy.

residents-only-property.rationale: Localist closure cuts against their globalism.

job-guarantee.rationale: Their four demands favour automation, a shorter week and unconditional income over guaranteed employment, so a job guarantee is not their route.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Not discussed; they want to capture and use state authority rather than disobey it.

non-intervention.rationale: Not discussed; their globalism is not a strict sovereignty doctrine.

industrial-unions.rationale: They want the unions rebuilt and widened to the precarious, but the craft versus industrial form is not discussed.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: Conspiracy theories about minorities are rejected by an anti-racist universalism.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Not discussed; they criticise family hierarchy but do not call for abolition.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Not stated; transparency fits left democratic aims, although the manifesto accepts secrecy in some organising.

local-production.rationale: The manifesto condemns the localism of folk politics and favours global-scale coordination.

informal-organisation.rationale: The manifesto rejects relentless horizontalism and calls for vertical authority and durable organisation.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Not discussed; globalism inclines against it.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Localism cuts against collective planning at a larger scale.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Collective control of the means of production leaves personal goods private, though the sources do not state it.

defeat-communism.rationale: They draw on Soviet planning and cybernetics experiments and build on Marxist traditions.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: Mixed provision resembles neoliberal reform, which they oppose.

religion-illusion.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from a secular Marxist heritage.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: The manifesto accepts that capitalism was once the engine of acceleration, while arguing that it now constrains productive forces.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: They tie gender hierarchy to a post-capitalist, post-work transformation.

socialized-care.rationale: Not discussed; shortened work and basic income are their routes, not public care services.

purge-loanwords.rationale: Cultural purism contradicts their global outlook.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small self-governing communities are what the manifesto calls folk politics of localism.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: They want to go beyond capitalism, a post-capitalist or communist direction, not a third way.

historical-land-claim.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from rejecting nationalism.

holocaust-denial.rationale: Contradicts their universalism and basic scholarship.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: Contradicts their dismantling of gender hierarchies.

suppress-opposition.rationale: They want a democratic hegemony, though they accept secrecy and verticality in organising.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: Contradicts their stance against imperial hierarchies.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Religious doctrine; contrary to their secular outlook.

participatory-democracy.rationale: The manifesto criticises direct, local horizontalism, though it also wants real democracy as collective self-mastery.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: They want to dismantle gender and race hierarchies together with class domination.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: Follows from their anti-hierarchy, anti-essentialist outlook.

assisted-dying.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from left liberal norms.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: They see themselves as a left project building left hegemony.

alienated-labor.rationale: Their anti-work stance and call to diminish work's role echo the alienation critique.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Religious dress rules are not discussed in the sources, and secularism and minority rights point in different directions.

ban-nda-harassment.rationale: Not discussed; consistent with anti-hierarchy aims.

social-market-economy.rationale: They consider neoliberal and social-democratic compromises insufficient and want post-capitalism.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: Not discussed; they want strong collective authority.

rich-first.rationale: They reject trickle-down logic and neoliberal development.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: Great-power blocs are not discussed in the sources.

interest-free-mutual-credit.rationale: Mutual credit banking is not discussed in the sources.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: They oppose austerity and neoliberal policy programmes.

domination-women-nature.rationale: They want mastery over nature while ending gender hierarchy, so the claim itself is rejected or at least contested.

reification.rationale: Fisher and the Marxist heritage treat capitalist forces as seeming to rule people, though not in this exact vocabulary.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: Their strategy to build left influence in media rests on the premise that wealth shapes media.

promulgated-standing-laws.rationale: Rule-of-law doctrine in this form is not discussed in the sources.

online-participation.rationale: Not discussed; they criticise horizontalism but embrace technology.

open-government-data.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from transparency and modelling needs.

interfaith-marriage-restriction.rationale: Contradicts their anti-hierarchy and secular views.

citizens-assembly.rationale: They say assemblies alone are insufficient, but sortition is not discussed.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: Religious reform is not discussed in the sources, which are secular in outlook.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Their programme is aimed at overcoming concentrated economic power.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: Consistent with anti-hierarchy aims, but not discussed.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: Not discussed; secular but not necessarily atheist promotion.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: Not discussed; their vertical authority emphasis cuts against abolition.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociational institutions are not discussed in the sources.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: They want state-guaranteed unconditional income, not charity.

term-limits.rationale: Term limits for politicians are not discussed in the sources.

vote-delegation.rationale: Not discussed; they are sceptical of direct forms but favour technology.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: They treat climate breakdown as the most critical threat; extinction risk in general is not discussed.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: Not discussed; follows from anti-hierarchy aims.

rent-control.rationale: Not discussed; consistent with anti-neoliberal aims.

abolish-ip.rationale: The manifesto attacks intellectual-property monopolies and the patent wars that they say block technological progress.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Nuclear basing is not discussed in the sources.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: Foreign basing is not discussed in the sources.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: They want income decoupled from work through basic income and automation, so neither principle is endorsed.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: Absolute pacifism is not discussed; the manifesto frames politics as conflict, so mild disagreement is inferred.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: Not discussed; Prometheanism implies malleability but sources do not say.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: Feminist theory of the category of women is not discussed beyond the general aim of dismantling gender hierarchies.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: Nationalist cult, not part of their programme.

culture-before-state.rationale: Their strategy builds hegemony and institutions with state power in view.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Administrative redrawing for one people is not discussed; their universalism makes it unattractive.

independent-unions.rationale: They want union renewal and independent class power, though autonomy from parties is not discussed.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: They build on a Marxist inheritance but stress a multi-class populist coalition.

second-chamber.rationale: Legislative design is not discussed in the sources.

confederal-coordination.rationale: Municipalist confederalism is a form of the localist horizontalism the manifesto rejects.

family-wage.rationale: Breadwinner family wage conflicts with their dismantling of gender hierarchy and post-work vision.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Not discussed; Promethean attitude toward technological progress.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Not discussed; Promethean rejection of immutable givens.

anonymous-payments.rationale: Cash-like digital payments are not discussed in the sources.

online-anonymity.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from left digital-rights stance.

person-over-state.rationale: Not discussed; they stress collective self-mastery.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: Devolution design is not discussed in the sources.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: Military doctrine is not discussed in the sources.

free-public-college.rationale: Not discussed; consistent with decommodifying provision and building left intellectual capacity.

pollution-taxes.rationale: Not discussed; they want climate action but via planning, not market tools.

future-generations.rationale: Their climate warning rests on avoiding ecological collapse.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Gender essentialism contradicts their anti-hierarchy aims.

arms-reduction.rationale: Armament levels are not discussed in the sources.

open-diplomacy.rationale: Secret versus open diplomacy is not discussed; the manifesto even allows secrecy in organising.

capital-controls.rationale: Not discussed; consistent with planning against neoliberal finance.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: The state's monopoly on arms is not discussed in the sources.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: Refusal of orders is not discussed in the sources.

collective-bargaining.rationale: They want union renewal; bargaining is not the central mechanism.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: They favour unconditional income over wage top-ups tied to work.

fiscal-rules-binding.rationale: Austerity-style fiscal rules contradict their programme.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: Not discussed; consistent with global post-capitalism.

smash-state-machine.rationale: The manifesto says the material platform of neoliberalism need not be destroyed but repurposed.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: They call for comprehensive post-capitalist planning, not a free multiplicity of local experiments.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Not discussed; natural capital accounting is a market framing they would not adopt.

internal-colonialism.rationale: Regional exploitation inside states is not discussed in the sources.

shared-human-nature.rationale: Prometheanism holds there are no immutable givens, so human nature may be redesigned, though the book keeps universal human values.

public-service-media.rationale: Not discussed; they want left influence in media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Their outlook is secular and rationalist, so a perennialist claim about religions is not one they would affirm.

farm-price-support.rationale: Agricultural policy is not discussed in the sources.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: Nuclear deterrence is not discussed in the sources.

workers-own-party.rationale: The book calls for a populist coalition and an ecology of organisations, not a single working-class party.

ban-fgm.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from anti-hierarchy aims.

one-language-many-names.rationale: Linguistic classification disputes are not discussed in the sources.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: A libertarian alternative to planning and collective action.

environment-over-liberty.rationale: Not discussed, though climate seriousness pulls toward it.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from left views on punishment.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: Language requirements for immigrants are not discussed in the sources.

voter-id.rationale: Not discussed; inferred from left democratic access concerns.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: State recognition of religious interpretations is not discussed in the sources.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: The manifesto says real democracy must be defined by its goal of collective self-mastery, not by procedures alone.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Contradicts their technological and democratic outlook.

negative-income-tax.rationale: They favour a generous unconditional income, not a tapering benefit designed to replace welfare.

women-suffrage.rationale: Basic equality; follows from dismantling gender hierarchies.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: Not discussed; secular but not a stated claim.

race-social-construct.rationale: Not discussed directly; consistent with dismantling race hierarchies.

gender-equality-agencies.rationale: Not discussed; consistent with anti-hierarchy aims.

homestead-ownership.rationale: A libertarian property theory opposed to collective control.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: International criminal justice is not discussed in the sources.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Not discussed; consistent with anti-hierarchy aims.

defend-planned-state.rationale: They study Soviet planning experiments, but their sources say nothing about defending bureaucratic states.

indirect-election.rationale: Indirect election through councils is not discussed; their stress on vertical authority is only a weak hint.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Ethnic territorial autonomy is not discussed in the sources.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: Plebiscites over disputed territory are not discussed in the sources.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: Post-colonial border policy is not discussed in the sources.

simple-living.rationale: Opposed to their Promethean abundance-through-technology aim and to the localist folk politics they criticise.

restrict-indigenous-settlement.rationale: Settlement restrictions in indigenous regions are not discussed in the sources.

equal-conscription.rationale: Conscription is not discussed in the sources.

close-ties-china.rationale: Foreign alignment with China is not discussed in the sources.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Not discussed; consistent with collective control of productive resources.

self-ownership.rationale: A libertarian doctrine opposed to collective post-capitalist aims.

cut-consumption-tax.rationale: Consumption taxes are not discussed in the sources.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: They favour universal unconditional income, not poverty targeting.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: They want organised, institutional politics rather than populist bypass of parties and groups.

no-business-privileges.rationale: Not discussed; consistent with anti-neoliberal aims.

national-resource-control.rationale: Not discussed; their globalism makes national control not a stated aim.

treaties-binding.rationale: The sources never discuss treaties with internal nations, and adherents have no shared line on them.

god-not-male.rationale: Not addressed in the sources; support is inferred from their aim to dismantle gender hierarchies within a secular outlook.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Blocking foreign purchases is economic nationalism, which sits poorly with their globalism, though they also oppose neoliberal deregulation.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: The sources never address religious texts, so this is left neutral rather than inferred.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Full automation and a reduced working week are two of the four demands of Inventing the Future and the manifesto calls for less work.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Its post-capitalist programme of basic income and shared automation gains judges distribution by outcome rather than by how wealth was acquired; inferred from those demands.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: The manifesto attacks neoliberal finance and wants to rebuild economic infrastructure, which fits taxing speculative finance, though the tax is not named; inferred.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Left accelerationists want a universal left hegemony and treat structural oppression as real, though they criticise identity-focused 'folk politics'; inferred from their left universalism.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: The sources do not discuss the authority of law; adherents' emphasis on building counter-power does not settle the question.

multipolar-world.rationale: The sources do not address world order; their universalist, global-scale politics points one way and their hostility to US-led capitalism the other.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: The Marxist inheritance suggests sympathy, but the sources argue about automation and a world without work rather than defend a labour theory of value; inferred and split.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: The manifesto rejects localism and favours a universalist, global project, so national patriotism is not part of its strategy; inferred.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inventing the Future criticises identity-based 'folk politics' but seeks a broad universal coalition that includes recognition struggles; adherents are split.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: The programme is for post-capitalist planning and a new left hegemony built through broad organisation, not for a ruling communist party or markets under one; inferred.

missingStatements.text: Society should automate most paid work so that people can work far less.
missingStatements.rationale: Full automation and a reduced working week are two of the four demands of Inventing the Future and the manifesto calls for less work.

missingStatements.text: The technology and infrastructure built under capitalism should be taken over and repurposed for collective ends rather than destroyed.
missingStatements.rationale: The manifesto says the material platform of neoliberalism need not be destroyed but redirected toward common goals.

notes: Many answers outside economics, technology and strategy are inferred from the movement's universalism and anti-hierarchy stance, so the profile rests on a narrow base of stated positions. Land's right accelerationism would answer most economic and democratic statements oppositely.
